messages:
Jules T.: Notifying folks  after the overnight RBAC refactor a bunch of SAST checks started returning "no owner resolved" and several DAST jobs failed with KMS:PermissionDenied. Also noticed a small audit log gap for the scanner SA.

Jules T.: sample logs:
```
2025-01-12T04:12:03Z sast: ownership-resolver: git read: 403 Forbidden
2025-01-12T04:12:04Z dast: unwrap secret: KMS PermissionDenied projects/redwood-inference/locations/global/keyRings/ci/cryptoKeys/artifact
```

Anika M.: cc @infra-ops @sec-oncall  which terraform change went out? I only approved a role consolidation plan.

infra-ops: We applied TF change that removed several broad group bindings and replaced them with scoped groups. During consolidation the scanner service account lost an explicit roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter and roles/source.reader binding (we relied on group membership that didn't include the scanner).

sec-oncall: Verify timeline and collect request IDs for the audit-gap. If logs are missing, export what we have and open a cloud support case. Also check whether scanner is using wrapped ephemeral keys that may get orphaned during rotation.

Jules T.: Gap around 2025-01-12T04:11:50Z - 04:14:10Z. Request IDs near the window: rq-x17 / rq-x18. Exporting current logs to gs://sec-exports/1777001234/partial/ now.

CI-bot: pipelines: queued re-run for affected PRs.

Anika M.: Immediate mitigation: re-grant explicit bindings to the scanner SA. Commands I ran:
```bash
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-inference \ 
  --member=serviceAccount:scanner-sa@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com \ 
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter

gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-inference \ 
  --member=serviceAccount:scanner-sa@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com \ 
  --role=roles/source.reader
```

infra-ops: Updated terraform modules to include explicit consumer bindings and bumped the sink retention to avoid accidental removal. Pushed plan to lock changes.

Jules T.: Re-runs: DASTs mostly passing; SAST still flags ~18 PRs as ownerless. Ownership-resolver returned 5xx/403 during the window and cache TTL propagated the bad state.

sec-oncall: Short-term pipeline adjustment: if ownership-resolver responds with 5xx/timeout, fallback to parsing in-repo CODEOWNERS and mark owner as OWNER:inferred (do not hard-fail). Open follow-ups to revert to strict enforcement after fixes.

Anika M.: I'll land a feature-flagged PR: owner_fallback=true with a metric emitted when fallback is used. PR will also add an alert: ownership-resolver error-rate > 0.5% for 5m -> P0.

infra-ops: Also adding pre-apply checks to the infra CI: verify all service accounts used by pipelines have explicit bindings listed in the plan and warn/abort if any removal affects these SAs.

Jules T.: Filing tickets: SEC-7001 rehydrate-scanner-iam, SEC-7002 owner-fallback-pipeline, SEC-7003 audit-log-cloud-support. Assigning infra + sec-oncall. I'll attach audit exports and terraform diffs.

payments-eng: Our payments PRs are impacted  we'll rebase when most checks are green. Ping me when backlog shrinks.

sec-oncall: If cloud support cannot reconstruct the missing logs, request forensic assistance (provide request IDs rq-x17/rq-x18 and sink name). Add runbook step: preserve wrapped keys and maintain temporary decrypt grants across rotations until consumers validate.

Anika M.: Also drafting a short postmortem + a checklist for RBAC refactors: 1) enumerate affected SAs 2) confirm explicit bindings survive TF changes 3) run integration test simulating KMS rotation 4) communicate window to product teams.

Jules T.: Thanks all. I'll keep this thread updated with ticket links and support case numbers. Please keep discussion to this thread for the incident record. :thumbsup:
